observation.visible_scene: A light wooden stick (dowel) lies horizontally across a setup on a gray sheet over a white surface. A row of standing cylindrical disc magnets sits in front of the stick and a second row of flat disc magnets behind it. Two hands grip the stick's ends at the start; later a single hand brings a small polished steel ball and sets it on the left end of the stick.
visible_changes: Frames 1-3: two hands hold the stick level over the magnets; the scene is otherwise static.
Frame 4 onward: the hands are absent and the viewpoint is more top-down; the stick and magnets remain still (frames 4-6 static).
Frames 7-19: a left hand enters holding the steel ball and slides/positions it along the left portion of the stick.
Frame 20-21: the hand opens and withdraws, leaving the ball resting on the left end of the stick.
Frames 22-26: the ball shows horizontal motion blur as it travels from the left toward the right end of the stick.
Frames 27-41: the ball comes to rest at the right end of the stick (near the last magnet), with only minor settling/position shifts between frames; the scene is otherwise static.
outside_clip_unknowns: The reason for the stick's placement and the magnet arrangement (no cause shown).
What occurs after the ball stops at the right end (clip ends before any further event).
Whether the ball's travel is driven by magnet attraction or by an initial push (the trigger is not visible).
uncertain_details: The abrupt change between frame 3 (angled view with hands) and frame 4 (top-down view without hands) may be an editing cut or a camera reposition; not confirmable as continuous motion.
Exact resting position of the ball in the final frames varies slightly frame to frame, possibly small oscillation or camera jitter rather than deliberate movement.
